statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays at 12% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green: a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

What changed this hour is the reading of the Hormuz off-ramp, and it changed for the worse. The Iran-Oman shipping framework credited last hour comes with two conditions Iran has stated publicly: it bars American and Israeli vessels from the strait, and it is contingent on Washington lifting its blockade of Iranian ports. On Thursday the United States said the opposite - that it could maintain the naval blockade of Iran indefinitely, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promising economic isolation "like have never been seen in the history" of such measures. As currently stated the accord and the US position are mutually exclusive. Last hour's framing of a genuine off-ramp was too generous; this is a bilateral arrangement the party that matters most has effectively pre-rejected.

Hezbollah's statement is now confirmed in its own words: the Israeli strikes "will be met with an appropriate response," with no timing or scope given, alongside a demand that Beirut stop what it called the "humiliating path of direct negotiations." That second clause matters as much as the first - it puts the negotiation track itself under attack, not just Israel.

Meanwhile oil, not equities, is where the conflict is actually being priced. WTI closed Friday at $82.40 (+1.4%) and Brent at $88.52 (+1.7%), both extending weekly gains of more than 5% on the blockade threat, while NQ finished at 30,141.75 (-0.15%) and the VIX at 14.25. That cross-asset divergence is the whole story, and it does not resolve until tonight's reopening auction.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item is scheduling, not sizing. The roughly 22:00 UTC restart sits inside the forecast window and is the single checkpoint that matters: forecast Tail steps to 22% at 22:00 UTC and 23% at 23:00 UTC, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) for the last three slots and holding at 22% into 00:00 UTC Monday. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment an entire weekend gets priced at once - an undelivered Hezbollah response, a Hormuz framework that is incompatible with the stated US position, a third struck ADNOC vessel, and a 5% weekly move in crude - against a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 12% and status green, but the Hormuz off-ramp reads worse on inspection - Iran's Oman accord bars US vessels and demands the blockade end, while Washington threatens to keep it indefinitely - so Stress rises to 73% into tonight's 22:00 UTC CME restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first twenty-one forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 69% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified against primary sources this hour: NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly reporting the contract closed as of 14 August. VIX 14.25, -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Fed's H.15 release at the 13 August observation. Nothing in that cross-asset set is aligned into a one-way equity structure. Conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail.

The material new information this hour is a correction to last hour's own reading, and it cuts one way rather than two.

Last hour credited the Iran-Oman shipping-map accord as the first genuine off-ramp since the tanker attacks began compounding, and marked Stress up by only one point as a result. On closer reading of the primary reporting that credit was too generous. Iran's own description of the arrangement carries two conditions: it prohibits American and Israeli vessels from transiting the strait, and it is contingent on Washington ending its blockade of Iranian ports. Both are load-bearing. And on Thursday the United States moved in precisely the opposite direction, warning it could maintain the naval blockade of Iran indefinitely while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration would "apply measures like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation on a country." A framework whose precondition the counterparty has just publicly refused is not an off-ramp yet. It may still become one - negotiations are described as forward-moving, the geographic coordinates of a safe route are agreed, and a joint coordination centre is under discussion - but it does not currently justify capping the compounding.

Oil confirms which market believes what. Crude rose above $82 on Friday, extending gains to more than 5% on the week specifically on the blockade threat, with Brent up 1.64% and WTI up 1.92% intraday. Energy has repriced the conflict continuously for a week. Equity volatility has not: the VIX closed at 14.25, near the low end of its 52-week range, and the Nasdaq Composite finished Friday about 0.3% lower while still closing the week higher. When one asset class prices a supply shock and another prices nothing, the honest place to record that is Stress, and the honest reading of the gap is that equities carry unhedged headline exposure into a thin reopening auction.

Lebanon is now confirmed in Hezbollah's own words rather than paraphrase. The group said Israeli attacks "will be met with an appropriate response," giving no timing, nature or scope, and added that Lebanese authorities "must not insist on continuing along the humiliating path of direct negotiations," accusing them of granting Israel free concessions. The strikes themselves killed eleven in Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani, including three children and two women, with nineteen wounded; the IDF says they answered a Hezbollah attack that seriously wounded three Israeli soldiers, and one strike was the deepest into Lebanon in two months. These are the deadliest exchanges since the June de-escalation. A promised, undelivered retaliation combined with an explicit attempt to collapse the negotiating track is a two-part overhang, and neither part can decay while markets are shut.

Why Tail stays at 12% and not higher: Tail measures a pathological price path, not the size of a pending headline stack. There is no path. The full amplifier checklist - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ pinned near an extreme, aligned yields, VIX, oil, semis, megacaps and breadth - is unobservable and stays unobservable for roughly another nineteen and a half hours. Publishing an elevated Tail now would assert structure that no venue has produced.

Why Stress rises to 73% (high) rather than the single point of recent hours: the de-escalation column that softened last hour's increment has largely been removed on closer reading, the escalation column is unchanged and still accumulating, and crude has now put a number on it. Stress stays inside the high band rather than moving to extreme because the framework negotiations are real and progressing, because no new physical incident was reported in this hour, and because a large but recoverable drawdown - not a regime break - remains the correct characterisation of the risk.

The horizon geometry is fully engaged. From 02:00 UTC Sunday the 24-hour forecast reaches 01:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC restart and the first three hours after it sit inside the window. Forecast Tail therefore drifts 12% to 19% through the halt and then steps to 22%, 23%, 22% and 21% for the final four slots, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. A thin opening auction absorbing an entire weekend at once is exactly the configuration in which gap continuation can outrun mean reversion. That is a conditional forecast, not an observation: the current published action remains EA_ON and green.

Confidence at 69% (solid) is up one point on evidence quality, not on any change in risk. Index, volatility, energy and rate marks are verified against primary sources this hour and are internally consistent; the Hezbollah statement was read in direct quotation rather than summary; the Hormuz conditionality was corroborated across independent reporting; and the seven-day US calendar was re-read directly from Trading Economics, confirming no US release of any kind before Monday's Empire State survey and no Fed event before Wednesday's FOMC minutes. But the single most informative input for a mean-reversion strategy - live price path - is structurally unavailable until the restart.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 02:00 UTC Saturday to 01:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours. Tail never left the low band, drifting 9% to 12%. Stress is what actually moved: 45% through the Saturday Asian hours, then climbing steadily through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54%, 55%, 56%, 58%, 57%, 60%, 62%, 65%, 67%, 68%, 70% and 71% as the Lebanon strikes were confirmed and turned into a two-sided exchange and the Hormuz tanker attacks accumulated. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 58% to 68% as primary-source marks were re-verified hour by hour. Action was EA_ON and status green for all 24 hours, and dominantMode was mixed throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 01:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first three hours after it are inside the window. Tail is held in the low band for 21 of 24 slots, drifting 12% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 22% at 22:00 UTC, 23% at 23:00 UTC, 22% at 00:00 UTC and 21% at 01:00 UTC Monday, where the forecast action becomes WATCH and the forecast status yellow. Stress grinds from 73% to a 78% plateau because unpriced weekend risk compounds while the venue is shut - an undelivered Hezbollah response, an explicit Hezbollah demand that Beirut abandon direct negotiations, a Hormuz framework whose precondition Washington has publicly refused, a third struck ADNOC vessel, and crude up more than 5% on the week - then eases to 76% once live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. Confidence eases from 69% to 62% as Friday's marks age past a hundred hours, then recovers to 67% once live quotes return at the reopen. The last seven slots switch to event/whipsaw to reflect a thin opening auction that has to absorb the entire weekend at once.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. CME equity-index futures remain in the weekend halt, so there is no live NQ path to score and Tail stays at 12% with the action EA_ON. Stress rises two points to 73% because this hour's reading sharpens rather than softens the picture: Iran's Hormuz framework with Oman is explicitly conditional on Washington ending its blockade of Iranian ports, and Washington spent Thursday threatening to maintain that blockade indefinitely. The off-ramp credited last hour and the US position are not compatible as currently stated.

Deep Asian-hours dead zone with every venue shut. No price discovery and no structural change expected; the only realistic mover is a fresh Lebanon or Hormuz headline landing into a market with no mechanism to reprice it for another twenty hours.
Unchanged halt conditions. Confidence begins its slow decay as Friday's marks age past eighty-five hours, which is an evidence-quality effect and not a risk signal.

Still no venue quoting. Hezbollah's promised 'appropriate response' to the Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani strikes remains undelivered, and its statement also pressed Beirut to abandon the direct-negotiation track - an overhang that cannot decay while markets are shut.

Sunday pre-dawn. Stress edges to 74% on pure compounding: three ADNOC vessels struck in under a week, a Saturday bulk-carrier hit, and Hormuz transits still near one ship a day against a roughly seventy-three per day peacetime norm.

Early European Sunday. Nothing tradeable, but this is roughly when weekend wire copy and any Israeli or Hezbollah statements tend to firm up, sixteen hours ahead of the reopening auction. Oil is the live transmission channel to watch: WTI closed Friday at $82.40 after a weekly gain of more than five percent while the VIX sat at 14.25.
